P2B-V1.tester: Root coordinator using supported Sky computer-use tools
orderedActionsAndActualResults: Normal Managed launch created player-a at Core revision 1/local count 0 with own offered options. Choosing fixed assassination plus bring_it_down committed revision 2/local count 1; explicit Refresh retained only the permitted own fixed mission and hid the opposing decision.

Hand off cleared the old board, session-ID field, mission, offered controls and receipt/error display. The opaque target-player-b curtain waited for explicit Ready and did not automatically reveal another view. Native controls complement the rendered evidence for outgoing state/roster invalidation.

Ready opened the same session at unchanged Core revision 2 as player-b/local count 0, with only player-b own offered options and no player-a private mission. Choosing tactical committed revision 3/local count 1; explicit Refresh retained the permitted player-b state.

Handing back cleared the display again. Ready restored player-a on the same session at Core revision 3/local count 0 with only player-a own fixed mission, no player-b tactical details, and the next own reserve options.
Alt+F4 closed the Game normally. Game and launcher exited 0 without forced cleanup; the Managed-owned Core receipt records STOPPED with forcedTermination false.
limits: Screenshots demonstrate the rendered display and root-observed ordered actions. Internal request counts, no mutation during handoff, current-viewer authorization and hidden state invalidation additionally rely on the native instrumentation and reviewed source; pixels alone do not establish those properties.
This is the bounded existing-workstation Windows Development Game workflow, not complete battle progression, clean-host Windows or Linux acceptance.
Roster DTO invalidation is covered by native/source evidence; this slice has no populated roster widget to visibly exercise.

P2B-V2.tester: Root coordinator using supported Sky computer-use tools
orderedActionsAndActualResults: First Attach launch used the child-only invalid-player-b diagnostic against the separately owned selected Core. Player-a created and chose fixed assassination plus cleanse at revision 2. The same session ID was copied privately with Ctrl+A/C before handoff; no private ID is published.

Hand off hid the old display. Ready for player-b showed the actual HTTP 401 authentication_required message: A valid bearer credential is required. Board, offered options, mission, ID and receipt remained absent; Ready retry stayed enabled and no automatic session was created. The client then closed normally with Game/launcher exit 0; the attached Core remained healthy at HTTP 200.

A fresh ordinary-credential Attach launch pasted the same privately copied ID with Ctrl+V and Open restored player-a at revision 2/local count 0, own fixed mission visible and opposing information hidden.

Clicking the board and sending wheel -240 visibly zoomed the board. Clicking the read-only ID field and Ctrl+A visibly selected its text; F retained the zoom. Wheel 600 over the panel also retained board zoom. The panel content fitted the window, so this verifies wheel isolation and does not claim actual overflow scrolling or persisted UIA field semantics.

Hand off restored the opaque curtain. A curtain click, wheel -240 and F kept it hidden, did not trigger Ready and did not give visible board focus. Ready for player-b then restored the same session at revision 2/local count 0, only own offered options and no player-a mission, with a fresh framed board.

Alt+F4 closed the second Attach client normally; Game and launcher exited 0 without forced cleanup. The separately owned Core again returned HTTP 200 before its owner stopped it normally with STOPPED/forcedTermination false. A final Sky list_windows observation found no Game window. The final read-only process check at 2026-10-25T03:47:42.5700495Z independently recorded zero Game processes and the shared owned Core STOPPED.
limits: The exact HTTP error is a root-observed UI result. Screenshots alone cannot establish the internal HTTP exchange or hidden camera internals; the matching native controls and source review provide complementary evidence.
The panel fitted the window: no overflow-scroll claim is made. Text selection proves the observed focus interaction only; no persisted UIA field semantics claim is made.
No physical RMB/MMB, actual OS switching/teardown, native Linux, clean-host Windows, complete P2 progression or additional unobserved action is accepted by these runs.
